summary: Desloratadine is a long-acting, non-sedating second-generation H1 antihistamine (the active metabolite of loratadine) used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria in patients 12 years and older. It is given once daily, has minimal CNS penetration, and the dose is reduced to every other day in hepatic or renal impairment.
indications: Seasonal allergic rhinitis - relief of nasal and non-nasal symptoms (>=12 years)
Perennial allergic rhinitis - relief of nasal and non-nasal symptoms (>=12 years)
Chronic idiopathic urticaria - relief of pruritus and reduction in number and size of hives (>=12 years)

dosage.n: May be taken without regard to meals

dosage.r: Adults with hepatic or renal impairment

admin: Take one 5 mg tablet once daily, with or without food
Orally disintegrating tablets: place on the tongue and allow to disintegrate, no water needed
Use measured oral solution for younger children per label
Take at about the same time each day
moa: Desloratadine is a long-acting tricyclic histamine antagonist with selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist activity. It inhibits histamine release from mast cells and does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier, accounting for its low sedative potential.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to desloratadine, loratadine, or any ingredient of the product

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk; animal studies showed no teratogenicity at exposures many times the human dose. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Desloratadine is excreted in human breast milk. Use with caution in nursing mothers, weighing benefit against potential infant exposure.
renal: In adults with renal impairment a starting dose of 5 mg every other day is recommended based on pharmacokinetic data; desloratadine is not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: In adults with hepatic impairment a starting dose of 5 mg every other day is recommended based on pharmacokinetic data.

moderate: Ketoconazole, erythromycin, azithromycin (raise desloratadine levels - no clinically relevant safety change)
minor: Other CNS depressants (additive sedation rarely, given low CNS penetration)
interactions.alcohol: No significant interaction at therapeutic doses; avoid excessive intake
interactions.diagnostics: Discontinue several days before skin allergy testing to avoid false-negative results

monitoring: Adjust dosing frequency in hepatic or renal impairment
counsel: Take once daily; it generally does not cause drowsiness
May be taken with or without food
Stop the medicine and seek care if you develop rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing
Stop several days before allergy skin testing
For orally disintegrating tablets, use dry hands and take immediately after opening the blister
pk: Up to 24 hours - supports once-daily dosing
Store at 25 C (77 F); protect from heat (avoid >=30 C) and light
pearls: Active metabolite of loratadine; non-sedating because it poorly crosses the blood-brain barrier
Once-daily dosing with a long ~27-hour half-life
Reduce to every-other-day dosing in hepatic or renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose is generally limited to somnolence at high single doses; no clinically relevant adverse events occurred in volunteers given 45 mg daily for 10 days. Management is supportive with standard measures to remove unabsorbed drug; desloratadine is not eliminated by hemodialysis. No specific antidote.
